### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. myofibrillar myopathy 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.730)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2389)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic CRYAB variants (HGVS:c.XXX) —DISRUPTS→ CRYAB (HGNC:2389); CRYAB (HGNC:2389) —PRODUCES→ Alpha-crystallin B (CRYAB) protein; Alpha-crystallin B (CRYAB) protein —DISRUPTS→ Cellular proteostasis and protein folding (GO:0006457); Cellular proteostasis and protein folding (GO:0006457) —LEADS_TO→ Protein aggregation (HP:0003209); Protein aggregation (HP:0003209) —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy (HP:0003212); Protein aggregation (HP:0003209) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638). Loss-of-function variants in CRYAB lead to impaired chaperone activity, disrupting cellular proteostasis and promoting protein aggregation. This aggregation underlies the myopathy seen in myofibrillar myopathy 2 and contributes to the cardiomyopathy observed in certain forms of distal myopathy.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in CRYAB with a clearly dominant-negative or gain-of-function mechanism for either disease, or the absence of any significant protein aggregation phenotype in affected tissues, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: The presence of common benign variants in CRYAB at a frequency >1% in gnomAD would suggest that the proposed causal variants are rare and specific.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of CRYAB in proteostasis offers potential therapeutic avenues targeting protein aggregation or enhancing chaperone activity to ameliorate symptoms in both distal myopathy and myofibrillar myopathy 2.

#### 2. fatal infantile hypertonic myofibrillar myopathy  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.728)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2389)

**Proposed mechanism:** CRYAB (HGNC:2389) —DISRUPTS→ Alpha-crystallin chaperone activity (GO:0005830); Alpha-crystallin chaperone activity (GO:0005830) —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy (HP:0003198); Alpha-crystallin chaperone activity (GO:0005830) —LEADS_TO→ Infantile hypotonia (HP:0001252). Loss-of-function mutations in CRYAB impair its chaperone activity, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins and subsequent myopathy. This shared disruption of alpha-crystallin chaperone activity underlies the myofibrillar myopathy observed in both conditions, with infantile hypotonia being a specific manifestation in fatal infantile hypertonic myofibrillar myopathy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in CRYAB with a gain-of-function or dominant-negative mechanism in either disease would falsify this hypothesis.

**Why it matters:** Targeting chaperone function or protein aggregation pathways could offer therapeutic strategies for both MONDO:0014073 and fatal infantile hypertonic myofibrillar myopathy.

**Proposed mechanism:** PIK3CA (HGNC:9523) —INCREASES→ PI3K-AKT-MTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP466); PIK3R2 (HGNC:9531) —INCREASES→ PI3K-AKT-MTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP466); AKT3 (HGNC:397) —INCREASES→ PI3K-AKT-MTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP466); MTOR (HGNC:7518) —INCREASES→ PI3K-AKT-MTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP466); PI3K-AKT-MTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP466) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal brain morphology (HP:0000273); PI3K-AKT-MTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP466) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability, severe (HP:0010804); CRYAB (HGNC:2574) —DISRUPTS→ PI3K-AKT-MTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP466).
